check_interval_ticks.description: How long to wait before checking a condition again while it does not hold. The first retry uses this interval, and every retry after that doubles it
check_interval_ticks.advice: Lower it to convert sooner after a condition starts holding. Raise it to check less often when many drops are loaded

backoff_max_ticks.description: The cap on that doubling. A condition that stays false waits at most this long before the next check
backoff_max_ticks.advice: Lower it so a rule that will hold later retries sooner. Raise it to save more performance at the cost of slower reaction

max_checks_per_tick.description: The checks-per-tick ceiling, used only while `max_work_units_per_tick` is absent
max_checks_per_tick.advice: Change it only when you want to control how many checks run per tick. Most servers never need this

overlay_directory.description: The name of the rule overlay directory, relative to `config/`, so rules live in `config/<this value>/rules/`
overlay_directory.advice: Change it only to rename the config directory. Move the whole directory with it, or the overlay rules stop loading. The location of `server.json` itself does not change

fabric_lifespan_fallback_ticks.description: Fabric only: the natural lifespan in ticks used until the current server run samples a reference drop lifespan
fabric_lifespan_fallback_ticks.advice: The default matches how long vanilla drops live. Adjust it only when the server changes drop lifespan rules

debug_logging.description: Whether the mod writes its run-time progress to the log, such as a drop whose condition does not hold and how many ticks until the next retry
debug_logging.advice: Turn it on temporarily while you diagnose why something does not convert. Keep it off otherwise, because it floods the log

server_budget_us.description: The time in microseconds the mod may spend per game tick. Work that does not fit continues over the following ticks
server_budget_us.advice: Lower it for extra safety on a busy server. Raise it when conversions lag and the server has spare capacity

max_work_units_per_tick.description: The total work-unit ceiling per tick. It applies together with `server_budget_us`, and whichever comes first wins
max_work_units_per_tick.advice: Leave it absent. Write it only when you need to set the work per tick on its own

effects_work_units_per_tick.description: The per-tick quota reserved for running effects, such as spawning items, placing blocks, and granting experience, so that heavy output does not crowd out the checks
effects_work_units_per_tick.advice: Raise it when a large batch of products takes too long to appear. Lower it to keep the checks prompt

check_spread_window_ticks.description: When many drops come due at once, the mod spreads those checks over a window of this many game ticks
check_spread_window_ticks.advice: Raise it when a simultaneous batch causes lag, which is smoother but delays individual conversions. Lower it to keep conversions on time when a single tick can take the load

dispatch_batch_size.description: How many queued conversions the mod advances per tick at most, and it also caps the returned items delivered in one batch
dispatch_batch_size.advice: Raise it when large batches back up

prepare_groups_per_step.description: How many groups one step prepares fixed effect inputs for during the preparation stage of a settlement, spreading the preparation of a whole stack over several game ticks
prepare_groups_per_step.advice: Lower it when many settlements start at once and preparation hitches a single tick. Raise it to start producing sooner for very large stacks, at the cost of more work per tick

new_product_protection_seconds.description: How many seconds a freshly converted product (dropped item, mob, or other entity) resists destruction by fire, lava, and cacti
new_product_protection_seconds.advice: Raise it when products burn as soon as they appear, for example next to lava. Set `0` to let products be destroyed right away

conversion_cooldown_seconds.description: How many seconds a freshly converted item cannot start another conversion
conversion_cooldown_seconds.advice: Raise it when products convert again immediately under another rule. Set `0` to let a product convert again at once

position_search_checks_per_tick.description: How many candidate positions the mod tries per tick when it looks for a spot for a product or a returned item
position_search_checks_per_tick.advice: Raise it when items stay undelivered because the terrain leaves few spots. Lower it to save performance

rescan_entities_per_step.description: How many loaded drops one step rebuilds when tracking is rebuilt after startup, a dimension load, or a rule reload. The rest continues over later ticks
rescan_entities_per_step.advice: Lower it when a server with tens of thousands of drops still hitches on a single tick after startup or a reload. Raise it to finish sooner, at the cost of more work per tick

cancels_per_step.description: How many queued tasks one step cancels when a rule reload, a dimension unload, or a server stop detaches them. The rest continues over later ticks
cancels_per_step.advice: Keep it at the default (or lower) when a reload or unload still spikes on a single tick. Raise it to finish clearing old queues sooner, at the cost of more cancel callbacks per tick

debug_scenario_prepare_batch_size.description: Affects only the preparation stage of test scenarios in a development environment, with no effect on normal play
debug_scenario_prepare_batch_size.advice: Players never need to change it

debug_scenario_prepare_budget_us.description: The time cap in microseconds for that same preparation stage
debug_scenario_prepare_budget_us.advice: Players never need to change it

settlement_recovery_max_attempts.description: How many times the mod retries a settlement that failed mid-run before giving up for this session and leaving the record for the next startup scan
settlement_recovery_max_attempts.advice: Lower it when a dimension stays unavailable for long and you would rather let the next restart take over. Raise it only when a settlement fails for reasons that clear up after a few seconds

max_place_block_radius.description: Largest `radius` a single `place_block` action may use; rules above it are rejected when loaded or saved
max_place_block_radius.advice: Raise it to let one action cover a wider area, but the cost of one placement grows with the cube of the radius, so keep it modest; lowering it rejects existing rules that now exceed the cap, so edit those rules as well

nearby_products.description: The nearby product limits. The count of products already nearby, together with the declared output per group, decides how many groups this settlement may open. See the next section
nearby_products.advice: Lower it when piled-up products cause lag. Set the matching limit to `0` to remove the cap

nearby_products.item_limit.description: The cap on the total number of nearby items of the same kind, counted by the item or item tag that would be produced

nearby_products.item_radius.description: The counting radius in blocks for the limit above, as a cube centered on the action output origin block with an edge length of 2 × radius + 1

nearby_products.entity_limit.description: The cap on the number of nearby entities of the same kind, counted by the entity type or entity tag that would be produced

nearby_products.entity_radius.description: The entity counting radius in blocks, with the same meaning as above

nearby_products.experience_orb_limit.description: A kept field. It stays in the file so existing configs keep working, and it no longer affects any conversion

nearby_products.experience_radius.description: A kept field as well. It maps to no counting radius at all

max_effect_offset_x.description: Maximum absolute trigger offset on the X axis per action, in whole blocks; defaults to 6. Set 0 to fix this axis at zero
max_effect_offset_x.advice: Reopen the editor after changing it. Loading and saving validate against the current limits; reduce offsets in rules that exceed them

max_effect_offset_y.description: Maximum absolute trigger offset on the Y axis per action, in whole blocks; defaults to 6. Set 0 to fix this axis at zero
max_effect_offset_y.advice: Reopen the editor after changing it. Loading and saving validate against the current limits; reduce offsets in rules that exceed them

max_effect_offset_z.description: Maximum absolute trigger offset on the Z axis per action, in whole blocks; defaults to 6. Set 0 to fix this axis at zero
max_effect_offset_z.advice: Reopen the editor after changing it. Loading and saving validate against the current limits; reduce offsets in rules that exceed them
